hook.line: Everyone promises things in this neighborhood: the work will be ready, the permit will come. You do not want to say "I don't believe you", only "let's wait and see".
hook.es: Dijeron que la obra estará lista en marzo; habría que ver si es verdad.
hook.en: They said the building work will be finished in March; we'll have to see if it's true.

examples.es: Dijeron que la obra estará lista en marzo; habría que ver si es verdad.
examples.en: They said the building work will be finished in March; we'll have to see if it's true.

examples.es: Habría que ver si nos dan el permiso.
examples.en: It remains to be seen whether they'll give us permission.

examples.es: Habría que ver si Altamira dice la verdad.
examples.en: We'd have to see whether Altamira is telling the truth.

examples.es: Dijeron que llega a las ocho; habría que ver si llega a tiempo.
examples.en: They said he arrives at eight; we'd have to see if he arrives on time.

rule:
*Habría que ver si* is a polite way to doubt something: it remains to be seen whether it is true. It never names who should check, so nobody gets accused.

After *si*, use a normal verb, as in English: *habría que ver si es verdad*, *si nos dan el permiso*.

It often follows a claim you have just heard: *Dijeron que… habría que ver si…*. There is no *que* after *si*, and no subjunctive.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an impersonal conditional used to express scepticism (*escepticismo cortés*).

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si es verdad.
options: We'd have to see if it's true.
It is true.
I saw that it's true.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si nos dan el permiso.
options: They gave us the permit.
It remains to be seen whether they'll give us the permit.
We must give them the permit.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si Altamira dice la verdad.
options: Altamira tells the truth.
We'd have to see whether Altamira is telling the truth.
Altamira would have to see the truth.

readAndPick.es: Dijeron que llega a las ocho; habría que ver.
options: They said he arrives at eight; we'll have to see.
He arrived at eight.
I know he arrives at eight.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si llega a tiempo.
options: It remains to be seen whether he arrives on time.
He arrives on time.
He should arrive on time.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si de verdad lo hizo.
options: He really did it.
We'd have to see whether he really did it.
He would really do it.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si es cierto.
options: We'd have to see if it's true.
It's certainly true.
I would like to see it.

readAndPick.es: Dijeron que la obra estará lista; habría que ver si es verdad.
options: They said the work will be ready; we'd have to see if it's true.
The work is ready.
The work was ready.

readAndPick.es: Habría que ver si te creen.
options: We'd have to see whether they believe you.
They believe you.
You would have to believe them.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *es* or *sea*, and type the whole sentence: We'd have to see if it's true.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si es verdad.
accept: Habría que ver si es cierto.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It remains to be seen whether they'll give us permission.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si nos dan el permiso.
yourTurn.why: *Nos dan* is the normal present; no subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We'd have to see whether Altamira is telling the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si Altamira dice la verdad.
yourTurn.why: The verb after *si* is the usual one.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We'd have to see if he arrives on time.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si llega a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: *Habría que ver si* plus a normal verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Add the doubt to the claim: *Dijeron que la obra estará lista.* They said the work will be ready; we'd have to see if it's true.
yourTurn.answer: Dijeron que la obra estará lista; habría que ver si es verdad.
accept: Dijeron que la obra estará lista, pero habría que ver si es verdad.
yourTurn.why: Put the claim first, then the doubt.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We'd have to see whether they believe you.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si te creen.
yourTurn.why: *Te creen* is the normal verb after *si*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We'd have to see if he really did it.
yourTurn.answer: Habría que ver si de verdad lo hizo.
accept: Habría que ver si lo hizo de verdad.

pitfalls.wrong: Habría que ver que es verdad.
pitfalls.right: Habría que ver si es verdad.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are asking whether, so you need *si*, not *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Habría que ver si sea verdad.
pitfalls.right: Habría que ver si es verdad.
pitfalls.why: No subjunctive after *si*; the verb stays normal.

pitfalls.wrong: Tendría que ver si es verdad.
pitfalls.right: Habría que ver si es verdad.
pitfalls.why: *Tendría que* needs a someone; *habría que* is for nobody in particular.

personal: Think of a promise you have heard lately and say *Habría que ver si…*.
